thread:
Leslie (support): heads up — multiple customers reporting p99 spikes and timeouts on text-generation endpoints in us-west after last-night infra deploy. several reports show 500s + token generation stalls.
DeployBot: deploy finished 2026-03-17T00:12Z commit: a7c9f2d -> infra/gpu-driver v0.58 + firmware nvlink-2.4.0 rolled to us-west-2.
Jordan (oncall): assign to eng-infra + sre. Any immediate mitigation we can push?
Raj (eng-infra): I saw the rollout. nvlink-2.4.0 had link retrain changes — plausible it increases PCIe lane flaps under heavy kv-cache stress. can we get kernel dmesg and nvme io stats from an affected host?
Emily (sre): grabbing logs now from host gpu-usw2-113. dmesg shows repeated: "nvlink: retraining link from speed X -> Y" and a bunch of "nvme0: I/O 0 timed out" around the timestamps of spikes. iostat shows nvme avg wait jumped from 1ms -> 20ms during repro windows.
Leslie (support): customer repro command: 
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-xxl","prompt":"test"}'
```
Typical: 0.12s, hitting affected host: 2.8s / sometimes 504.
Jordan (oncall): can we route traffic away from nodes with nvlink errors? quick fix: cordon nodes and drain, fallback to older instance pool.
Raj (eng-infra): yes — tagging affected nodes and moving them out of autoscaling group. command: 
```
kubectl label node gpu-usw2-113 infra/rollback-needed=true
./infra-tools/drain-and-migrate --label infra/rollback-needed=true --dest-pool legacy-gpu-pool-usw2
```
Emily (sre): also seeing 1-2 hostfs stall events tied to heavy KV cache writes during infill batches. Suggest temp mitigation: reduce max_batch_size for gpt-xxl on us-west route and enable immediate fallback to model-variant quantized-8 to reduce I/O.
Leslie (support): informing affected customers: status page update with ETA ~2h while we rollback the driver in us-west and validate.
Jordan (oncall): decision: rollback gpu-driver to v0.57 + nvlink-2.3.1 in us-west, put canary on 3 nodes, run repro load, then full rollback. Raj/Emily own rollback runbook.
Raj (eng-infra): starting canary rollback on gpu-usw2-121/122/123 now. command run: 
```
infra-deploy rollback --component gpu-driver --version v0.57 --zone us-west-2 --nodes gpu-usw2-121,gpu-usw2-122,gpu-usw2-123
```
DeployBot: rollback job queued (job id: rollback-7954321). ETA ~12m per node for restart and health checks.
Emily (sre): will monitor dmesg + iostat + request p99. adding temporary Grafana panel to show nvlink retrain rate + nvme avg wait over 1m windows.
Leslie (support): opened incident report to CS with links to repro and customer logs. sending proactive heads-up to top-tier customers.
Jordan (oncall): if rollback doesn't stabilize, second-order mitigation: throttle kv-cache write bursts (decrease async write workers), pin affected customers to dedicated capacity, or enable routing to eu fallback pool.
Raj (eng-infra): noted. after canary looks good, we schedule full rollback across us-west pool and then re-run validation suite: 1) synthetic p99 load, 2) kv-cache saturation test, 3) couple customer repros.
Emily (sre): preliminary canary results: after driver rollback on gpu-usw2-121, nvlink retrain events dropped to 0 and nvme avg wait back to 1.1ms, request p99 fell from 2.8s -> 0.14s. rolling to remaining nodes.
Leslie (support): customers updated. one customer already confirmed latency normalized for their traffic.
Jordan (oncall): action items: Raj — complete rollback and run full validation (OWNER). Emily — keep monitoring + postmortem skeleton. Leslie — CS communication + post-incident customer notes. ETA 2.5h for full rollback.
Raj (eng-infra): starting full rollback now. will post updates in this thread.
DeployBot: rollback-7954321 status: 3/150 nodes completed, 12m elapsed.
Emily (sre): thumbs up on the rollback working on canary. continuing to watch for any residual hostfs stalls.
Leslie (support): thanks everyone — closing high-touch CS escalations as customers confirm. will collect customer repros and attach to postmortem. :thumbsup:
